newsitem.title: INDIA: India says China helps Pakistan build warheads.
newsitem.headline: India says China helps Pakistan build warheads.

text.p: India has accused Pakistan of developing nuclear warheads for medium-range missiles with China's help.
New Delhi has also said Pakistan may have deployed M-11 ballistic missiles near the Indian border.

A lawmaker in the upper house of parliament asked Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral in a written question if the government "are aware of Pakistan's developing of nuclear warheads for its medium-range missiles with active technical assistance from China".
Junior Foreign Minister Saleem Iqbal Shervani responded in a written answer released by parliament on Thursday: "Yes, sir."
Another member of parliament asked Gujral if the government had verified reports that Pakistan had deployed Chinese-built M-11 missiles near the India border.

"Government are aware of credible reports in this regard," junior Foreign Minister Kamala Sinha replied in writing. "The acquisition of missiles and related technologies by Pakistan is being continuously monitored and assessed by Government."
The accusations were made public as India and Pakistan celebrated a half century of independence.
Last week, India accused China of supplying M-11 missiles to Pakistan and helping its arch foe build a missile factory.

It was believed to be the first time India had publicly and unambiguously accused China of supplying M-11 missiles to Pakistan. The United States voiced deep concern over the reported supply of Chinese missiles to Pakistan.

The U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) concluded last year that China had delivered to Pakistan 30 ready-to-launch M-11 missiles, each capable of carrying a 1,100-lb (500-kg) warhead more than 185 miles (300 km).

Both Pakistan and China have denied reports of missile transfers. Islamabad has dismissed fears voiced in the United States and India about its alleged missile development, saying it was doing nothing contrary to its commitments.

In July, Pakistan tested a Hatf-series missile, believed to be medium-range. India later said it planned to build the controversial intermediate-range Agni missile that was mothballed last December, apparently under pressure from Western countries that opposed its missile programme.

Gujral was asked by a member of parliament in a written question if the government was aware of "Pakistan's acquiring nuclear warheads for its medium-range missiles", as reported in an Indian daily last month.
"Yes, sir," Shervani responded in writing. "Government is deeply concerned over reports in the Pakistan media that Pakistan has test fired a medium-range missile."
India moved a small number of Prithvi surface-to-surface missiles near the Pakistan border earlier this year, but has said it did not deploy the weapons, which have a 250-km (150-mile) range.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since independence in 1947. The two launched peace talks in March, but since then have periodically traded accusations.
